findings.summary: onError resolves the error correctly into the local `error` variable and logs it correctly, but the final `return maybeError as Promise<void>;` returns the raw second parameter instead of `error`. In the single-arg call shape (`onError(err)`) — the shape the code's own doc comment says the SDK actually uses — `maybeError` is `undefined`, so the hook returns `undefined` instead of the resolved error. Since the SDK does `throw this.onError(e)`, this means the rethrow carries `undefined` for exactly the primary call shape the brief asked to fix, silently losing the real error at the DO boundary. The two-arg shape happens to work only because `maybeError` and `error` are the same value in that branch.
